subject: Evidence and walkthrough: where requests are executed, subprocessor roster, and cross-border transfers
messages:

Date: Tue, 25 Jun 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q: where do Redwoods LLM requests run? evidence for cross-border transfers

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — HealthWave liked the latency profile. Legal asked me to capture a couple of specific items before we proceed:

1) Where exactly do inference requests execute for the hosted API (regions and typical hops)?
2) Which subprocessors (cloud providers, networking partners, monitoring) may touch request payloads or telemetry?
3) For a US-only deployment requirement, can you guarantee no cross-border processing, or is a Dedicated/Private deployment required?
4) What are typical retention windows for request logs, KV cache, and any persisted payloads? If we require deletion on request, what is the turnaround time and evidence we can expect?

Could you provide an evidence pack (diagram + subprocessor roster + short notes on SCCs/SAs) that I can share with Legal? We may need this for their vendor review.

Caroline Morris
Head of Platform Partnerships
HealthWave
caroline.morris@healthwave.com

Subject: Re: Quick Q: where do Redwoods LLM requests run? evidence for cross-border transfers

Hi Caroline — great to hear feedback, and absolutely we can put an evidence packet together. High-level answers up front so you have something for Legal while we pull artifacts: 

- Regions / execution: Redwood hosts inference in multiple regions. For the hosted API we run execution pools in: US West (us-west-2), US East (us-east-1), and EU West (eu-west-1). By default requests are routed to the optimal pool (latency/cost) but we support region pinning for customers who need execution locality.

- Subprocessors: primary execution substrates are AWS (EC2/GPU instances), GCP for some managed services, and a small set of networking/CDN providers (Fastly / Cloudflare) for routing. We also use a managed monitoring provider (Datadog) and a logging archive partner (S3-compatible storage). The attached CSV lists the current roster and primary contact/region.

- US-only guarantee: If you need a strict US-only processing commitment for inference, we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private (VPC) where we can guarantee execution pools are in customer-controlled US regions and disable routing to EU pools. For hosted customers we can apply a US-routing policy but that is not the same as an isolated Dedicated pool.

- Retention / deletion: ephemeral data (token-level KV caches) is kept in-memory and evicted per runtime SLOs; request traces and logs are retained by default for 30 days. We offer enterprise retention controls (custom TTLs) and an erase-on-demand process — typical verified deletion takes up to 72 hours once the request is validated. Full details and exports will be in the pack.

I'll attach a simple data-flow diagram and the subprocessor inventory; Marissa will follow up with the SCC/SAs and SOC2 evidence references. Would you be available for a 30-min call Wednesday to walk Legal through the packet?

Best,
Aisha
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Quick Q: where do Redwoods LLM requests run? evidence for cross-border transfers

Hi Caroline — thanks for the note. I'm attaching the short evidence pack and answering the bullets inline: 

1) Execution hops / regions
- Hosted: execution pools operate in us-west-2 (primary GPU fleet), us-east-1 (secondary), and eu-west-1 (EU pool). Requests are routed by smart-routing (latency + cost + quota). We can create a routing policy to prefer US pools but hosted customers share multi-region capacity.
- Dedicated/Private: we can provision Dedicated pools isolated to US regions (full data locality), or deploy Private on-prem/VPC for an air-gapped option.

2) Subprocessors that may touch payloads
- Compute: AWS (EC2/GPU) — primary execution; limited GCP used for batch evaluation jobs.
- Networking: Cloudflare (ingress/routing) / Fastly (CDN for web assets).
- Observability: Datadog (metrics/traces — traces can be configured to strip request payloads in the prod pipeline).
- Storage: S3-compatible object store (for artifacts and customer uploads) — encryption at rest.

Note: For hosted inference, the only subprocessors that may execute model inference are our cloud compute providers (AWS/GCP) inside the listed regions. The CSV lists contact, region, and contractual status (SCC / DPA).

3) US-only guarantee
- For a contract-level US-only processing guarantee you should select Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private. For hosted customers we can apply a strict US routing policy and operational controls, but hosted remains a multi-region service and cannot provide the same isolation guarantees required for some regulated contracts.

4) Retention and deletion
- KV cache: ephemeral in-memory; evicted within minutes to hours depending on workload. Not persisted to long-term storage.
- Request logs / traces: default 30 days; enterprise customers can request shorter or longer retention.
- Deletion on request: verified deletion of any persisted artifacts and logs is completed within 72 hours after a validated request. Deletion of in-memory cache is immediate but cannot be historically verified (because it was never persisted).

Evidence & controls
- We attach: data-flow diagram (redwood_data_flow_v2.png), subprocessor inventory (subprocessor_inventory_20280625.csv), and a short memo with SCC/DPA references and SOC 2 pointer. For EU transfers we rely on SCCs and will share executed DPAs on request. We also support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/Private deployments.

If HealthWave's Legal wants an explicit statement for the contract, we can produce a short addendum describing the isolation model for Dedicated (execution-only in US regions + KMS key residency).

Next steps: Aisha — feel free to share the zipped evidence pack. Caroline — if helpful I can join the call and walk your Legal team through the diagram this Wednesday.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Infrastructure Security
